title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the second part of the 'Longue Marche' sequel (ms. p. 311), on 'loop groups' (groupes à lacets): discrete or profinite groups with a privileged family of conjugacy classes of inertia ('lacets') indexed by a set I, modelling π_1 of a surface of type (g,ν). The previous page went from a type (1,1) structure to a type (0,3) one: take E minus its 2-torsion E[2], quotient by ±1 to get a sphere minus 4 points, then 'plug the hole' at the image i_0 of the origin. This page starts the inverse functor, the 'torus group' functor.

Step 1. Start from π̃ in Ẽ: an exterior loop group of type (0,4) with a marked inertia index i_0. Then I(π̃) = {i_0} ⊔ I(π), where π is the (0,3) group obtained by filling i_0, so |I(π)| = 3.

Step 2 (65). Let T be the orientation module (Ẑ(1) or Z). The abelianization of π̃ is generated by the four inertia classes, and (π̃_ab)⊗Z/2 is described through (Z/2)^{I(π̃)}.

Step 3 (66)-(67). There is a canonical character π̃ → Z/2: the one taking value 1 (the nonzero element) on every inertia generator. Equivalently it is the 'sum of coefficients' map (Z/2)^4 → Z/2. Topologically this is the double cover of P^1 branched at the 4 points, i.e. the Legendre/Weierstrass elliptic curve.

Step 4. The kernel π̃' is π_1 of E minus E[2], a loop group of type (1,4). Each puncture is ramified, so it has a single preimage, giving I(π̃') ≅ I(π̃), as stated in (69) on the next page.

Step 5 (subtlety). π̃' is not a well-defined exterior group 'up to inner automorphisms' of itself. Conjugation by elements of π̃ outside π̃' induces the extra outer Z/2 action (the involution -1 of E). So π̃' is defined only modulo inner automorphisms together with this Z/2 symmetry.

Step 6 (next page). Filling the three punctures indexed by I(π) leaves i_0 as the origin, giving a type (1,1) group with its canonical ±1 action. This is a 'symmetrized' object, slightly less than an object of C^ext_{1,1}. To get a genuine object one must choose a lift, i.e. a group in the exterior class of π̃.

The problem served is comparing the categories of exterior loop groups of types (0,3)/(0,4) and (1,1), the two basic 'building blocks' of the Teichmüller tower, compatibly with the Galois/GT actions.
errors: (65) as written, π̃_ab ≅ T^{I(π̃)}, is inaccurate. For type (0,4) the abelianization is T^{I}/T: the sum of the inertia generators (suitably oriented) is zero, so the rank is 3, not 4. Likewise (π̃_ab)⊗Z/2 ≅ (Z/2)^I/diagonal ≅ (Z/2)^3. The sum-of-coefficients map (67) still descends, since the diagonal (1,1,1,1) sums to 0 mod 2. The argument is therefore unaffected; probably shorthand or a slip.
The notation (π̃_ab)_2 presumably means π̃_ab ⊗ Z/2. As written in (67) the arrow to (Z/2)^I should go the other way, or be onto a quotient, given the correction above.

ideas.what: Elliptic curve as the double cover of P^1 branched at 4 points: π_1(E∖E[2]) is the kernel of the canonical character of π_1(P^1∖4 points) that is nontrivial on all inertia generators.
ideas.modern_name: Legendre family / Weierstrass double cover; relation between M_{0,4} and M_{1,1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Legendre, Jacobi, Klein); in the anabelian/GT setting Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme singles out M_{0,4} and M_{1,1} as basic pieces; the explicit construction is likely in La Longue Marche (1981)

ideas.what: The kernel of the canonical character is an exterior group only modulo the additional outer Z/2 (the -1 involution): a 'symmetrized' exterior group of type (1,1), which needs a choice of lift to become an object of C^ext_{1,1}.
ideas.modern_name: exterior group with ±1 symmetry; stacky nature of M_{1,1} (generic automorphism -1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Nakamura's work on profinite (1,1) and Out-groups

ideas.what: Functorial equivalence between categories of (marked) exterior loop groups of type (0,4)/(0,3) and type (1,1), via the plug/unplug operations.
ideas.modern_name: comparison of the GT-actions on Γ_{0,4} and Γ_{1,1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse) as programme; worked out by Lochak, Nakamura, Schneps

missed.claim: This is a categorical, functor-level treatment of the passage (0,3)/(0,4) ⇄ (1,1) for abstract 'groupes à lacets'. It explicitly isolates the obstruction that the result is only a ±1-symmetrized exterior group. This is a precise unpublished formulation, but the underlying mathematics is well known.
missed.quote: ce n'est pas tout à fait un groupe extérieur - il n'est pas défini à automorphisme intérieur près, mais seulement modulo (en plus) l'opération extérieure des symétries de Z/2Z
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is relevant to axiomatic, stack-theoretic treatments of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller tower, where the ±1 automorphism of M_{1,1} must be handled. Likely only of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, routine construction: the elliptic double cover of the 4-punctured sphere, phrased in Grothendieck's loop-group language. Its content (the M_{0,4}–M_{1,1} relation and the ±1 subtlety) is well known in the GT literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads: 'Le foncteur "groupe des tores": un groupe (π̃ ∈ Ẽ) à lacets extérieur (de type (0,4)), muni d'un élément i_0 ∈ I(π̃) tel que…'.
In (64) the underbrace under I(π) reads 'cardinal 3'.
'remplie' is uncertain. The meaning is the condition that the character equal 1 (be nontrivial) on all i ∈ I(π̃), perhaps 'valoir 1' or 'non triviale'.
'mais ce n'est pas [...] : fait un groupe extérieur' should read 'mais ce n'est pas tout à fait un groupe extérieur'.
'défini "modulo intérieur [?]"' should probably read 'défini "à automorphisme intérieur près"'.
The last line reads 'l'opération extérieure des symétries de Z/2Z' (the involution), continued on the next page with 'dessus'.
